mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship holds consistently across historical data.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction that reduces economic growth expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong industrial expansion (INDPRO > 102.5), rising manufacturing output supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 102.5, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates labor market strength that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1400 thousand units signals housing sector contraction that reduces economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is below 1400, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger manufacturing output that supports economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
